title: I turned business requirements into a complete Meta Quest VR game using AI + Godot
author: Tiny_Raisin9155
selftext:
A few weeks ago, I had a slightly crazy idea:

I’m an IT professional, but not a game developer. Writing requirements, testing software and figuring out what a product should do, however, is something I’m very familiar with.

So I wanted to find out: **What happens if I treat an AI like my development team?**

I started describing the requirements for a simple VR Sudoku game and used Astra to implement them in Godot.

The workflow basically became:

**REQUIREMENT → IMPLEMENTATION → TEST → FEEDBACK → NEW VERSION**

I defined what I wanted, tested everything directly on Meta Quest, reported bugs and changes, and kept adding new requirements.

And, of course, the “simple Sudoku experiment” got slightly out of hand. 😄

It now has multiple environments and difficulty levels, missions, medals, a Daily Challenge, local highscores, different music, board positioning, German/English support and more.

The result is **MiLeVR Sudoku**, and it actually made it all the way to a commercial release on the Meta Horizon Store for Quest 2 and Quest 3.

What surprised me most wasn’t simply that AI could generate code. It was how well a workflow I already knew from traditional IT projects translated to AI-assisted game development.

I still wouldn’t call myself a Godot developer. But apparently I can define, test and iterate on a game well enough to actually ship one.

And that leaves me with a question I find genuinely interesting:

**If I define the product, requirements and design, make the decisions, test every iteration and approve the result — while AI writes a large part of the implementation — what exactly is my role?**

Product owner? Designer? Developer? AI game developer? Something new?

I’d be very interested to hear how others here approach this.

If you want to see what eventually came out of the experiment:

https://www.meta.com/experiences/app/1313400305193617/?hwsh=ve3PgknmfF&utm\_source=twilight&utm\_medium=SHARE&utm\_parent=SHARING&utm\_cohort=ORGANIC\_UNKNOWN

**Also, I have 5 Meta Quest keys available. If anyone here is genuinely interested in trying the game and seeing what came out of this AI-assisted development workflow, just send me a DM. I’d be happy to share them with members of this community.**

comments.author: DivineMage1
comments.body: I don't have an answer to the role question, but I've had a very similar experience (also IT professional that isn't a game dev)

comments.author: daddywookie
comments.body:
I was a Product Owner in various sectors, most recently in a games studio. I had a similar experience to you and continue to,work on various games as a hobby.

I think the role you are looking for is Game Director. It has many of the same behaviours, defining the overall shape of the game and having the final say on what passes into production. I don’t know if AI Game Director will ever become a recognised role, it has the same whiff of self promotion as “CEO and Founder”.
